title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach to estimate the causal effect of COVID-19 lockdown orders on retail store foot traffic. The DID method is suitable because we have a treatment group (stores in counties with strict lockdowns) and a control group (stores in counties with minimal restrictions), and we can compare the change in foot traffic before and after the lockdown (March 2020) for both groups.

The key assumption in DID is that, in the absence of the treatment, the treatment and control groups would have experienced parallel trends in the outcome variable (foot traffic). This assumption can be checked by examining the pre-treatment period data.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(plm)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv")

# Convert the data to a panel data structure
pdata <- pdata.frame(data, index = c("unit_id", "period"))

# Estimate the DID model using fixed effects
fe_model <- plm(y ~ post + treat_x_post, data = pdata, model = "within")

# Print the coefficient for the interaction term (treat_x_post)
summary(fe_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]

# Robustness check: Clustered standard errors
coeftest(fe_model, vcovHC(fe_model, type = "HC1"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient for the interaction term (treat_x_post) to be negative, indicating that stores in counties with strict lockdowns experienced a larger decline in foot traffic compared to stores in counties with minimal restrictions after the lockdown. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the actual data, but we expect a substantial decline in foot traffic due to the lockdown measures. The parallel trends assumption can be checked by examining the pre-treatment period data, and if the assumption holds, the DID estimates will provide a credible estimate of the causal effect of the lockdown on retail foot traffic.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
